title: Define validation timing and focus-preservation behavior for multi-step/composed inputs
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: Complex inputs (composed fields like phone number split into country / area / number, address blocks, multi-part code entry, and selects with dependent toggles) currently have inconsistent validation timing and focus behavior across the library. Some components validate on blur, others on submit, and server-side errors sometimes move focus unexpectedly or hide the field that needs correction. This results in poor keyboard/AT flows and increased support tickets for form failures.

Goal: Establish a consistent, accessible pattern for validation timing (debounced soft validation vs authoritative validation), and define how keyboard focus and visible focus ring should be preserved or moved when validation messages appear, for both single-step and multi-step/composed inputs. The spec should be implementable by engineering, testable by QA, and cover error announcements for screen readers, motion tolerances, and token-level spacing changes if the UI grows/shrinks when messages are shown.
acceptance_criteria: A single decision doc exists that prescribes soft vs hard validation triggers for all form primitives
Focus behavior described for: inline validation on blur, on-change soft validation, and submit-time server errors
Accessible error announcement pattern defined (aria-live region strategy and focus anchoring) and examples for screen readers

Edge cases documented: field groups where an inline error collapses UI, validation on dependent fields (e.g., select enabling additional inputs), and multi-part inputs where only one segment is incorrect
Figma components + tokens updated with error height/spacing variants and motion specs for message reveal/slide (or crossfade) linked
Implementation tasks and ENG dependencies enumerated and handoff package created (PRD + component specs + QA checklist)
design_notes:
Initial research: reviewed production support logs (2 months of form failures), ran 8 moderated usability sessions with keyboard/voice users, and audited the current component library. Patterns observed: (1) users expect the focus to remain in the field they were editing when an inline validation appears; forced focus jumps cause confusion, (2) server-returned errors need a consistent anchor behavior so screen reader users can reach the failing field quickly, (3) multi-segment fields (card number, phone) benefit from segment-level error state but require a summarizing message for assistive tech.

Recommendation summary: use a two-tier validation model — soft validation (on-change debounced or on-blur) that surfaces suggestions/warnings without stealing focus; authoritative validation (on submit or server response) that may move keyboard focus to the first invalid control and place focus-visible on the control, with an aria-describedby relationship to the error text. For multi-part inputs keep segment-level aria-invalid flags and create a hidden live region with a concise summary plus an anchor link to the first invalid segment. For dependent inputs (select->toggle->subfield), perform validation top-down and avoid collapsing the element that receives focus; if collapse is unavoidable, set focus to the next logical focusable element and announce the change.

Tokens and spacing: define an error-message token set (error-height-xs/sm/md) so layout shifts are constrained. When possible prefer overlay/stacked messages that don't change input vertical position; when stack is used, animate with a 120ms ease to reduce vestibular issues.
decisions: Adopt two-tier validation model: soft (on-change debounced / on-blur) vs authoritative (submit/server)
On authoritative errors, move focus to first invalid control for keyboard users; for soft errors do not move focus
Implement a standardized aria-live 'polite' region for soft messages and 'assertive' only for server-critical errors that require immediate attention
For multi-segment fields keep segment-level aria-invalid and expose a concise top-level summary in an aria-live region
Prefer non-layout-shifting error affordances where possible; when layout shift is necessary use a constrained tokenized height and short motion
Document token names: token.input.errorMessageHeight.{xs,sm,md} and token.motion.errorReveal.short
tasks: Finalize decision doc and share with ENG/PM/design reviewers
Create Figma variants for TextField, Select, Toggle, MultiSegmentField with error token states
Prototype aria-live and focus behavior examples with simple HTML playground for screening by accessibility reviewers
Write component-level acceptance criteria for Frontend (aria attributes, focus preservation, animation timing)
Pair with ENG on an integration spike to validate server-error focus flow (ENG-21914)
Author QA testcases and keyboard/screen-reader test checklist
